title: Connect the stopped pause to a predictable walking exit
stage_label: Separate instructional session · Week 3, Day 1 · individually authored
status_note: Complete written athletic prescriptions with source and independent programming review. Consult the daily review and separate numeric results for verification scope. Current canonical release, actual facility/athlete evidence and precise separate tumbling remain unverified.
brief: Connect an actually controlled stop to the early-announced ordinary walking exit. The first progression is a full 2 s stopped pause to 1 s at the same actual approach, direction and geometry. Direct repeatable same-context 1 s work may be retained. Full-pause instruction, terminal stopping and stationary options preserve useful participation when the changed task is unavailable. Static stance fills the knee/unilateral role; familiar hip, push, pull and independently suitable brace follow.
quality_target: Observe a real bilateral stop before timing the selected pause, orderly exit-side opening steps with feet/body turning together, ordinary walking and a quiet separate finish. Record the actual approach, direction, pause, control, prompts and response. A shorter pause without a stable stop is not success; one observed direction or first changed attempt is not repeatability of another task.
continuity: Actual OR03/07/direct corresponding stop and direction-specific exit plus the most recent independent Strength/response records → one justified pause change or retained/component instruction → OR13 and OR20 require their own actual task/rule evidence. OR12, OR14 and OR15 retain their distinct planned objectives; this lesson does not pre-complete them.
audience: Ages 12–14 are the reference, not beginners. Every age has explicit standard/compressed D/L and within-age alternatives. Experienced arrivals can demonstrate relevant competencies without repeating all on-ramp visits. Current readiness, history, attention, growth-related changes, sport/tumbling exposure and restrictions determine each domain; older age never supplies a cut or load prerequisite.
readiness: Read each actual task and role record, not the attendance date. First 1 s requires repeatable corresponding 2 s; retained 1 s may use direct repeatable 1 s. First full 2 s exit needs actual corresponding stop plus ordinary turn/walk components. P2 checks walking only. Review recent sport, tumbling, impact, grip, attention and symptoms independently. Preserve smaller total opportunities, side-specific stance holds and compatible Strength doses. A new main pause grants no new load or support complexity.
equipment_space: PLANNING ONLY: 15 preparation bays and the five inspected wall stations, three 15 m straight preparation lanes with their own outside returns, plus individually fitting press/row/floor supports from OR03. Exact quantities: five stable wall positions, five incline supports, five benches and manageable single DBs for rows, five mats; breathing needs five leg supports, suspension needs five verified anchors. The main new exit uses ONE dedicated 6 m-wide ×15 m-long shared teaching area centered on the middle lane; the adjacent two approach lanes are CLOSED and incorporated into the protected exit area. Three lanes do not mean three simultaneous exits. Preserve the 15 m straight overrun, with no queue or apparatus ahead. Two 1 m-wide one-way returns are centered at lateral ±4 m, outside the active ±3 m area. Overall main active/return width is9 m plus separate waiting banks, rear paths and coach access. A2 m exit at45 degrees adds about1.414 m laterally and forward. With actual pause lateral position within±0.5 m, the outward path to matching return center is at most3.086 m; planning clearance allowance3.1 m. This is route arithmetic, not a safe-width guarantee or a foot-placement pass quota. Verify body/arm/fall room, exact finish position, surface, overrun and every path. If actual position or path does not fit, stop/reconfigure/defer; do not force the child onto a marker. Separate rear holding banks accept left/right returners without a shared merge. Next athletes feed behind the start boundary through a distinct front staging path. Keep P2’s three independently segregated preparation returns separate from the two main returns: the main area is closed during P2. After the last P2 return is clear, close all three preparation returns and transfer/reconfigure during the opening five-minute main setup; no P2 returner is sent into a merged two-path system. These spaces need not share a footprint. Pre-position both walking and jogging markers; the five-second main gap contains no marker relocation. Provide a separate2 ×3 m observation pad centered approximately6 m left of the main centerline and7 m forward, wholly outside the active fan and return strip, with additional verified access. The0.5 m gap beside a return is not a coach bay. Coach1 must actually see the complete foot/body sequence at either finish. Behind the start, keep independent left/right holding banks inside the outer returns, nominally lateral-3.5 to-0.5 m and0.5 to3.5 m, longitudinal-9.5 to-2 m, each with space for the full group if all return that side. Returners enter only at the rear near-10 m; bank fronts feed toward the central on-deck point near-1 m. No rear arrival crosses the other bank or a front feed. The ordinary staging path is at most8 m behind the start and takes up to10 s under the traffic coach; inspect the actual path and space before using this model. All transfers fit the stated setup windows. All dimensions, equipment, staffing and operating pace are unverified. Stationary E1 routes use separately identified personal preparation bays outside the active fan, all returns, holding banks and staging paths. Any transfer from P2 back to that bay occurs within the opening five-minute main setup. Each selected stationary bay must be fully visible from Coach1’s observation pad without crossing a live path; if that arrangement does not fit, omit or defer that route under this schedule. Familiar two-DB hip additionally requires five individually fitting elevated parking stations and ten simultaneously suitable DBs. Use the actual retained pair, parking height and range for each athlete. The 20 s inter-group hip reset is a planning allowance for verified station changes, not proof that arbitrary swaps fit. Pre-stage qualified equipment in the opening allocation; if a real change exceeds the allowance, delay the next group and omit later work rather than shorten handling or rest.
coaching_flow: Two qualified coaches: one observes the single complete main movement; the other controls staging, both outside returns and waiting banks. Only one athlete crosses the start at a time. Announce side before release. The next named traveling athlete may spend up to10 s staging behind the start boundary during the prior slot or opening setup; the first traveling athlete stages during19:50–20:00 standard or14:50–15:00 compressed. The inspected staging path is at most8 m, from the selected bank front to on-deck, wholly behind the start; this ordinary transfer never enters the active area or a return path. The prior complete action must clear before release. Returned athletes enter the rear of their side’s holding bank, with no merge across the active area or next-athlete feed. Coach2 may be monitoring up to two returning athletes and one staging athlete. Observe actual sightlines, spacing and path availability; this simultaneous traffic demand is an operating condition, not a staffing guarantee. If both roles cannot be supervised, pause releases. Numbered early opportunities may be delayed or omitted; no hidden walkthrough or make-up work is added. Position/standing athletes remain in their own inspected personal bays for E1; they do not join central on-deck staging or the outside return. Coach1 observes their10-second action in the same numbered25-second release slot, with no simultaneous main movement. Coach2 continues traffic control. Bay visibility and separation are required before mixing stationary and traveling routes; no zero-time transfer to the center is assumed.
clock: Explosiveness / controlled stop and walking-exit connection
time_rules: Earliest releases are a model, not a pace requirement. Demonstrations, support/lane checks, reset, recovery, water and transitions are included. Pre-position both approach marker sets during opening setup; no marker changes occur in an active five-second observation gap. No cueing interval is filled with extra athlete repetitions. A fault consumes its attempt; no make-up work. If actual logistics overrun, reduce uncompleted later attempts/supporting volume or leave the affected domain unresolved and record why.
preparation_note: Preserve the full resolved instructional base and its concluding hinge/squat observations. Exactly two targets occupy 180 s: P1 supported stance/quiet finish 90 s, P2 straight walking stop 90 s, with explicit stationary alternatives. Opportunity 1 of E1 contains the first complete selected task; no extra whole 2 s or 1 s exit is added to preparation.

exercises.name: Retain the supported stance and quiet finish
exercises.mapping: SPLIT-ISO-SUP plus bilateral orientation; SPLIT-STANCE-HIGH-TEACH when mid-range entry is unqualified
exercises.set_purpose: One short both-lead rehearsal retains the actual supported position and a separate bilateral finish before the stop/exit lesson. Quiet standing replaces it when the stance is not currently suitable; no split entry is claimed.
exercises.execution: Use the assigned stable wall station. Turn the body so the front-leg-side hand rests lightly on the wall at comfortable waist height; free hand at hip. Lead foot stays whole, rear forefoot on floor. Enter the already qualified comfortable mid-range, left lead then right lead, with3s each; stand fully to switch lead and support hand. Finish in a comfortable bilateral soft-knee base for2s with wall contact, then exit to the adjacent queue. Unknown mid-range entry/exit uses the high-stance branch at a small comfortable knee bend. This is a composite, not one exact source212 exercise.
exercises.cues: Light hand; front foot whole; breathe; stand to switch; two-foot finish.
exercises.errors: Calling both feet on the floor single-leg balance, gripping/leaning heavily into the wall, forcing depth, changing support hand without standing or taking extra practice reps.
exercises.rationale: The retained static position prepares knee/hip and trunk organization without another dynamic squat set, load change or support-removal lesson.
exercises.metadata: Method: one counted position comparison. Tenets: Balance/Body Control/Coordination. Pattern: supported split stance plus bilateral finish. Equipment: five verified wall stations.

exercises.competency: Use actual comfortable entry/exit, wall contact, depth and breathing. Preserve each lead’s smaller recent hold independently. P1 may use its quiet-standing alternative independently of later S1 eligibility; a preparation observation neither overwrites Strength history nor proves unsupported turning. When the actual familiar support/depth/entry is currently established but longitudinal hold duration for a lead is unknown, use at most 1 s on that eligible lead as a current planning cap and leave its historical duration null. The other lead retains its own known smaller ceiling. Unknown duration alone does not force first-high instruction. Known zero or an ineligible lead does not permit this positive both-lead packet: use eligible quiet P1 and defer S1; preserve independently useful other roles.
exercises.progression: Keep one combined rehearsal and the actual fitting support/depth. Each lead is at most the listed 3 s and its actual recent compatible hold. Explicit lead packets preserve asymmetry. A missing or painful action is omitted, never repaired with extra work.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03/07 or direct static stance record and current response → one retained/reduced P1 → separately eligible S1 and later OR13/20 observations; dynamic OR10 squat history is not stance seconds.

exercises.name: Retain the straight walking stop
exercises.mapping: WALK-STOP — proposed walking variant, explicit local lesson; no-travel position alternative separately labeled
exercises.set_purpose: One counted straight walking stop checks comfortable approach, gradual braking and bilateral finish. It prepares the stopping component without an extra whole exit before the first assigned main opportunity.
exercises.execution: Start from rest in the marked lane, walk2m with relaxed arms, begin slowing at the2m cue before the marked2.5–3m brake area, and stop with both feet in the3–4m finish. Use several comfortable steps, hold2s, then take ordinary walking steps through the marked side exit beside the finish into that lane’s own return path. This reset occurs after the terminal hold; it is not an athletic cut or timed redirect. The4–8m protected clearance and remaining lane to15m stay unobstructed for an overrun; they are not mandatory P2 walking distance. Do not walk back toward the next athlete inside the active lane.
exercises.cues: See the slow-down space; shorter steps; two-foot finish; hold; walk out.
exercises.errors: Waiting until the finish to brake, reaching for a hard final plant, imposing a left/right plant quota, continuing into a turn or mistaking runoff for extra braking space to aim at.
exercises.rationale: The full base plus two targets uses the whole preparation budget. The first complete selected main task is opportunity 1 of E1; no extra full-pause screen increases a one-opportunity athlete’s work.
exercises.metadata: Method: one predictable approach/stop rehearsal. Tenets: Balance/Coordination/Body Control. No intentional jump event; ordinary walking/braking steps still count.

exercises.competency: Comfortable ordinary walking and conduct permit counted walking-stop instruction. The completed P2 result can establish only its observed walking-stop component. It proves no jog stop, whole exit, opposite direction or repeatability of either pause context. Use independently suitable position/standing or defer if walking is unavailable.
exercises.progression: Retain one 2 m ordinary approach, gradual stop in the actual fitting region and 2 s bilateral hold. Ordinary side-gate clearance is logistics, not a directional test.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03/07 or direct walking/stop record → one counted straight component rehearsal → independently selected E1 route; OR13/20 receive only actual observed task-specific evidence.

exercises.name: Connect the controlled stop to the announced walking exit
exercises.mapping: PAUSED-EXIT-TEACH: complete OR11 proposed context snapshot; terminal and stationary alternatives retain separate mappings.
exercises.set_purpose: Opportunity 1 teaches or checks the selected complete task at the assigned pause and direction. Remaining numbered opportunities practice the independently eligible side-specific task with full reset and feedback. The primary change is a 2 s to 1 s stopped pause where justified; first full-pause instruction or retained/terminal work remains productive when that change is unavailable. Every fault consumes its opportunity.
exercises.execution: Announce the athlete and left/right before release. Retain the actual ordinary 2 m walk or qualified gentle 5 m jog, original gradual braking region and bilateral stop. Start the selected 1 s or 2 s pause only after real balance; if stabilization takes longer, do not race the cue. Open with the exit-side foot, let the other foot lift/replant and follow as feet and body turn together into the retained 45-degree, 2 m ordinary walking exit. Finish quietly on two feet for 2 s, then clear outward to the matching return when directed. No fixed-foot pivot, crossover, late cue, running exit or acceleration. If stopping fails, do not attempt the exit: preserve the straight overrun, stop the affected sequence and record partial work. The lane end is not a forced braking deadline.
exercises.cues: Direction first. Stop and balance. Hold the assigned pause. Open, let the other foot follow. Walk and finish. Wait for clearance.
exercises.errors: Timing the pause while still braking; racing the one-second cue; dropping the actual stop; fixed-foot twisting; changing approach or angle with the pause; transferring left evidence to right; restoring reference counts after smaller recent work; extra screening or fault repayment.
exercises.rationale: A shorter positive pause connects owned components while preserving a real stop and ordinary stepping. Retain the full-pause task when it is still being learned. Immediate cutting has different actions and prerequisites; the library’s fatigue-oriented deceleration repeatability method does not describe this finite recovered lesson. Static stance then fills the knee/unilateral role, with independent hip, push, pull and brace maintenance.
exercises.metadata: Method: finite technical opportunities with qualified observation, feedback and full reset; descriptive organization, canonical method ID unverified. Tenets: Agility, Coordination, Balance and Body Control. Explosiveness here teaches braking/redirection prerequisites; no high-output cut, sprint or jump is prescribed.

standard_D.variant: Stop, Pause and Announced Walking Exit — first 1s, walking approach

exercises.competency: FIRST 1 s: actual repeatable corresponding 2 s stop/opening-step/exit at this approach, geometry and direction plus current suitability; no prior successful 1 s trial is needed. RETAINED 1 s: actual repeatable same-context 1 s evidence plus current suitability, with no reconstructed older 2 s requirement. FULL 2 s first instruction: actual controlled corresponding stop and comfortable ordinary standing/turning/walking components; prior perfect whole exit is not required. A new jogging stop stays terminal-only. Each actual direction has its own evidence; P2 walking supplies neither jog-stop nor whole-exit repeatability. Symptoms, restrictions, distress, unsafe traffic or loss of control end the affected action; select an independently eligible retained/terminal route only in remaining original slots or defer. Direct retained jogging-stop/exit evidence does not require reconstruction of an older walking-stop record. The actual controlled corresponding jog stop, exact same approach/exit intent and whole-task context, ordinary walk/turn components and current suitability still govern; walking-stop prerequisites remain required for first jogging-stop instruction.
exercises.progression: Standard D: at most 3 opportunities; compressed D: 2; standard L: 2; compressed L: 1, further capped by actual compatible smaller history. First/opposite/first is the three-slot direction order; shorter doses take its prefix. Each side independently selects first_1s, retained_1s, full_2s, terminal or defer. If the other side is unavailable, its slot is not reassigned as extra work on the first side. Neither a single first 1 s success nor calendar attendance proves repeatability. L uses walking or stationary routes; D does not automatically restore jogging, counts or load. If 1 s control deteriorates, restore a suitable held task or end; the attempt remains counted. If longitudinal opportunity count is unknown but the selected task is independently eligible, use one original counted opportunity or omit it. This is a conservative current planning cap, not a claimed reduction from a known prior dose. Keep historical count null. An actual known smaller/zero count or applicable restriction governs; a missed visit is not invented completed zero work.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03/07 or direct stop and side-specific exit evidence, plus recent OR06–10 response → first or retained 1 s connection only where independently justified, otherwise explicit full-pause/terminal instruction → OR13 adds no cue complexity without its own movement/rule gates; OR20 verifies the actual retained variant without automatic reactive-cut clearance.

exercises.name: Retain the actual supported static stance
exercises.set_purpose: One combined both-lead hold preserves the actual knee/unilateral and trunk-control task after the main instruction. It occupies the knee role; no extra bilateral squat set is added. Independently suitable first high-stance entries are counted inside this set.
exercises.execution: At the verified wall, use the same recorded front-leg-side hand at comfortable waist height and free hand at hip. Lead foot whole, rear forefoot on floor. Enter the declared comfortable mid-range with rear knee hovering, hold with normal breathing, stand and switch lead/support hand in10s, repeat, then return to bilateral standing.15s total initial setup/entry and final exit are included. No repeated lowering/rising during a hold. Choose the shallow high-stance adaptation if mid-range entry/exit is unqualified; do not call tall/shallow standing the exact mid-range variant.
exercises.cues: Light support; own this depth; front foot whole; breathe; stand before switching.
exercises.errors: Dropping to an unqualified depth, rear knee resting, rear-foot elevation, full bodyweight leaning through the hand, shaking/straining to finish a timer or double-counting the two leads as two sets.
exercises.rationale: Support and comfortable depth keep this role distinct from today’s shorter main pause. OR10 dynamic goblet work informs cumulative response but does not prescribe static hold duration or remove support.
exercises.metadata: Method: instructional isometric, explicit reduction from source2×10–30s/side. Tenets: Strength/Balance/Body Control. Two feet supported; this is not a single-leg balance test.

standard_D.notes: One combined both-side set, not two sets. Two counted holds×5s +10s stand/change lead/support hand +15s total initial setup/controlled entry and final exit = 35s. exercises.competency: Mid/high requires actual comfortable controlled entry, breathing and exit at that depth with the lead-side hand lightly on a fitting stable wall, free hand at hip. First high stance may be taught from suitable comfortable standing, support and direct instruction; its first entries are counted, not an extra screen. Unsuitable entry ends the role. Unknown P1 stance can remain quiet while S1 independently teaches the high stance; quiet P1 does not force or qualify S1. When the actual familiar support/depth/entry is currently established but longitudinal hold duration for a lead is unknown, use at most 1 s on that eligible lead as a current planning cap and leave its historical duration null. The other lead retains its own known smaller ceiling. Unknown duration alone does not force first-high instruction. Known zero or an ineligible lead does not permit this positive both-lead packet: use eligible quiet P1 and defer S1; preserve independently useful other roles.
exercises.progression: One combined set, D at most 5 s each lead or L at most 3 s, with actual smaller side-specific holds retained. Explicit packets preserve left/right differences, support and depth. A planned age/mode ceiling is not permission to lengthen a recent hold. No dynamic split squat, external load or support removal.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR03/07 or direct static stance plus current response → one explicitly retained/reduced or first-high set → OR13/20 retain that actual setup; OR10/14 bilateral squat histories remain separate.

exercises.name: Retain the familiar hip pattern
exercises.mapping: HINGE-BW; independently familiar TWO-DB RDL alternative retains DB-RDL mechanics
exercises.set_purpose: One independently eligible hip set preserves useful full-body participation at the actual familiar setup and smaller dose. It complements the stop/exit lesson without a second load, handling or support progression.
exercises.execution: Default: arms crossed at chest, soft knees, hips back3s and stand1s through owned range,5s setup/exit. Familiar DB alternative: actual retained pair at individually fitting elevated parking positions. Hold one DB in each hand with palms inward and arms long; establish a comfortable tall top start with weights near the thighs. Hinge through the owned comfortable hamstring-limited range, with no floor-touch or forced stretch target;4s controlled pickup, three-second lowering/one-second standing repetitions,4s controlled set-down and2s clear. Soft knees, organized trunk, weights remain close; no wall touch, new reach target or grip/handling test. Record kg per DB, total load and actual parking height/range. First-time pickup/top-start/hinge/set-down instruction is not available in this loaded route.
exercises.cues: Keep the owned setup. Hips back. Stand smoothly. Park both weights under control when using them.
exercises.errors: Restoring old DBs after more recent unloading; assuming a firstOR06 teaching set proves familiar handling; one implement substituted for two; a new load or longer set; rushed handling or an extra trial to choose the route.
exercises.rationale: Stance first fills the knee/unilateral role, then hip, push, pull and brace proceed sequentially with explicit recovery. These roles preserve distinct movement practice; no superset, hidden test or extra circuit fills waiting time. A missing role does not erase independently suitable other roles.
exercises.metadata: Method: retained or reduced supporting hip practice. Tenets: Strength and Body Control. Bodyweight good morning or independently familiar two-dumbbell RDL; exact identity and handling remain distinct.

exercises.competency: Bodyweight requires an actual currently familiar comfortable hinge pattern and setup. Missing longitudinal dose history may use its at-most-2-rep packet only after that independent current familiarity/control is observed; it is not permission for a first unfamiliar hinge lesson, and an actual smaller 1-rep history governs. Familiar DB is D-only and requires actual most-recent compatible loaded hip evidence at the same pair/load/count, established controlled pickup/top-start/repetitions/set-down and suitable response. One first-DB set does not prove familiar 10 s handling. A newer unloaded record blocks older-load restoration. Five fitting elevated stations, ten simultaneously suitable DBs and direct two-coach observation must fit. Select eligible BW before pickup or defer if unavailable; faults consume the set without replacement.
exercises.progression: Retain the actual setup, range, load and compatible smaller count. A low packet persists in D if that is the current dose; further exact caps preserve smaller work. No new implement/support instruction in hip, push or loaded pull. The brace alternative has its own component entry. If an independently suitable listed route is unavailable, defer that role and arrange targeted instruction at a suitable later allocation. Faults consume the set and never generate replacement work.
exercises.continuity: Actual most recent compatible OR06–10/direct hip record and current response → one explicit retained/reduced OR11 set → OR12 and later relevant lessons apply their own objective and actual history; OR14 changes prompting/flow, not automatic demand.

exercises.name: Retain the familiar pull pattern
exercises.set_purpose: One independently eligible pull set preserves useful full-body participation at the actual familiar setup and smaller dose. It complements the stop/exit lesson without a second load, handling or support progression.
exercises.execution: Place opposite hand AND knee on the suitable bench, other foot planted. Pull1s, hold the top1s, lower2s; park and change sides in10s.10s total pickup/set-down is included. Count both sides within one set.
exercises.cues: Hand and knee supported; quiet trunk; pull smoothly; lower and park.
exercises.errors: Hand-only standing row, torso twist, unsuitable bench, dropping the implement or treating8total reps as8each side.
exercises.rationale: Stance first fills the knee/unilateral role, then hip, push, pull and brace proceed sequentially with explicit recovery. These roles preserve distinct movement practice; no superset, hidden test or extra circuit fills waiting time. A missing role does not erase independently suitable other roles.

exercises.name: Retain the familiar brace pattern
exercises.set_purpose: One independently eligible brace set preserves useful full-body participation at the actual familiar setup and smaller dose. It complements the stop/exit lesson without a second load, handling or support progression.
exercises.execution: Supine on the mat, arms fixed vertical, hips/knees in comfortable tabletop. Lower one bent leg until a light heel contact at the selected target, return, alternate.2s out/2s back. Tabletop check is setup; first listed contact is the counted moving-limb observation.
exercises.cues: Quiet trunk; light heel; return; keep breathing.
exercises.errors: Heel slide, straight-leg reach, moving the opposite arm, forced floor depth or extra reps to test readiness.

timing_narrative:
**Preparation, full base plus 180 s targets.** Use the complete instructional base below: 720 s standard or 420 s compressed. P1 is 90 s: 10 s gathering, 5 s reminder, five-athlete groups at 15/40/65 s. A full rehearsal is 5 entry + 3 left hold + 5 standing side/hand change + 3 right hold + 2 bilateral transition + 2 bilateral hold + 5 exit = 25 s. Actual smaller lead holds shorten only their phases; quiet P1 is its separate 10 s own-bay action. P2 is 90 s: 5 s gathering, 5 s reminder, three-athlete waves at 10/22/34/46/58 s; 10 s walking action (2 approach + 3 gradual brake + 2 hold + 3 ordinary side clearance), then 15 s independently segregated return. Last return ends at 83 s. Same-lane headway 12 s may overlap outside returns; verify spacing/view. P1-to-P2 completion gaps for the full supported packet are 46–72 s, not a claimed 60 s rest between targets. S1 keeps its own recovery rule. If the three simultaneous P2 observations cannot be supervised, omit the affected action and use existing direct evidence or counted main terminal instruction; no fabricated completion.

**Main setup and finite opportunities.** Standard 15–20 or compressed 10–15 includes demonstration, direction/context selection, transfer, inspection, closure of the two adjacent lanes, preparation-return closure and staging. The main uses one 6 m × 15 m shared fan, not three simultaneous exits. No P2 returner enters the two-return main system before reconfiguration. Pre-position walking/jog markers; no marker relocation fills a release gap. Opportunity 1 is the first whole selected task; demonstrations add no athlete attempts. The first traveling athlete stages in the last 10 s of setup. Later traveling athletes use at most 10 s behind-start staging in the prior numbered slot under coach 2; stationary athletes remain in separately inspected visible personal bays.

Full 2 s exit action: walk 2 approach + 3 brake + 2 stopped pause + 4 opening steps/entire 2 m ordinary exit + 2 quiet finish + 7 ordinary outward clearance = 20 s; jog is 3+3+2+4+2+6 = 20 s. A 1 s pause changes only that phase and leaves 8 s walking or 7 s jogging clearance slack, still 20 s total. There is no extra distance or faster gait target. The pause begins after control; an actual need for more time delays the next release. The 2 m exit at 45 degrees adds about 1.414 m laterally/forward; with an actual pause within ±0.5 m lateral and a matching return centered at ±4 m, outward clearance is at most 3.086 m, rounded to the 3.1 m planning ceiling. These are route calculations, not safe-width or foot-placement guarantees. Preserve the straight overrun for a failed stop.

Release one athlete every 25 s at offsets 0,25,…350. A 20 s action is followed by up to 45 s outside return: up to 35 m ordinary walking in 40 s plus 5 s rear-bank rejoining. Actual shorter paths are not padded to a distance quota. Last action ends 370 s and last return 415 s after round start. Two returners may overlap for 20 s on one outside path, while coach 2 also controls the next behind-start athlete; actual sightlines, no passing, bank capacity and separation must support this. One coach observes the full main action, the other controls traffic. Any delay stops later releases. Stationary actions use their own 10 s no-travel packet within the same single numbered observation slot, with no central staging or return.

Standard rounds start at 20/27/34 minutes; compressed at 15/22. D uses at most 3/2, L 2/1, with actual 1/2 caps omitting later slots. Seven-minute spacing leaves 355 s after a full 20+45 s action/return, exceeding the 60 s minimum. Last full D return is 40:55 standard or 28:55 compressed. Remaining time is feedback, water and Strength setup, never extra testing. A missing side uses an independently eligible terminal task in its assigned remaining slot or is omitted; it does not buy another first-side attempt.

**Strength and transitions.** Standard: stance 45–53, hip 53–58, push 58–63, pull 63–69, brace 69–75. Compressed: stance 35–41, hip 41–44, push 44–47, pull 47–51, brace 51–55. All are sequential whole-group roles, not circuits or supersets. Stance groups of five start 120/210/300 s into its standard block or 90/165/240 s compressed; one combined set at most 35 s, with initial setup included before those starts. Hip standard starts 60/120/180 s; compressed 45/95/145 s. A familiar two-DB set is at most 26 s including 10 s handling, followed by 20 s complete inter-group reset; last compressed work ends 171 s within 180. Bodyweight hip is at most 21 s. Push starts 60/120/180 s standard or 45/85/125 compressed, at most 17 s. Pull starts 90/160/230 s standard or 60/120/180 compressed, at most 52 s including side change and handling. Brace starts 60/140/220 standard or 45/100/155 compressed, heel taps at most 26 s or supported breathing 40 s plus 15 s quiet recovery. Last compressed row ends 232 of 240 s; breathing plus recovery ends 210 of 240 s. The compact hip delay still leaves at least 134 s from completed hip work to that athlete’s push, exceeding the familiar DB 90 s requirement. Other role changes preserve at least 60 s. Two coaches observe two/three familiar athletes per group; first high stance needs actual appropriate direct instruction and may delay/omit later work. All physical transfers, changes of support/load, setup, water and recording must fit the listed allocations. Real slower handling/teaching removes later unfinished work, never required rest.
alternatives:
**Choose the actual route before its counted action.** The complete first-1-second walking packet below is conditional, not a group default entitlement. For every age, first_1s needs repeatable corresponding 2 s work; retained_1s needs repeatable corresponding 1 s work without older-history reconstruction; full_2s first instruction needs actual corresponding stopping plus ordinary turn/walk components. Jog exits also require a currently owned corresponding gentle-jog stop; a new jog stop stays terminal. Record each direction’s context independently. Changing a pause does not introduce a new approach, angle, exit speed or strength load. The complete proposed source context is in the linked mapping; its current approval is unverified.

**Explicit main doses for every age.** Standard D 3 × 1, compressed D 2 × 1, standard L 2 × 1, compressed L 1 × 1, before actual smaller total caps. Exit walking: 2 m ordinary approach about 2/10, gradual brake/finish in the fitting 2.5–3/3–4 m regions, assigned 1 s or 2 s stopped pause, 45-degree 2 m ordinary exit about 2/10 including opening steps, separate quiet 2 s finish, then ordinary clearance/return. Qualified jog-exit is D only with the actual 5 m gentle approach about 3/10, 6–8 m brake/8–10 m finish region and identical walking exit. Both have a 20 s active envelope plus 45 s return and at least 60 s recovery after both. Natural relaxed arms and feet/body turning together remain. Actual recent slower approach or smaller count persists; D is not a request to restore jogging.

**Terminal and stationary main options, every age.** Independently eligible jog-stop D3/2 or walk-stop D3/2,L2/1 keeps its original corresponding approach/gradual brake and 2 s bilateral hold, then ordinary straight clearance through the protected walking 4–8 m or jogging 10–15 m overrun and outside return. Its shared-area allowance remains 20+45 s, with 60 s recovery. First jogging-stop instruction requires suitable actual easy jogging and controlled walking-stop components; it supplies no exit. Position option: one 10 s cycle per assigned opportunity, 3 s comfortable partial-squat lowering, 2 s bilateral hold, 1 s stand and 4 s reset, comfortable forward arms, bodyweight easy 2/10, at least 5 good repetitions in reserve. Standing: 2 s settle, 2 s quiet bilateral hold, 6 s reset, relaxed arms/unlocked knees and minimal effort. Both are no-travel own-bay tasks, D3/2,L2/1 or smaller total, 60 s recovery. P2 has one corresponding 10 s action; walking P2 adds 15 s return, stationary P2 none. Independent suitability is required; no available action means defer. Intentional jumps are zero, actual natural contacts unknown.

**Side order and count retention.** Record first side left or right. Three opportunities are first/opposite/first; two first/opposite; one first only. Apply actual compatible total before selecting each side’s context. A side without one-second permission may still learn/retain an eligible full-pause exit. If no exit is suitable, its original slot may use the independently eligible terminal route or be omitted, never another attempt reassigned to the first side. Faults and early starts consume their slot; record partial actions and actual pause. A single observation supplies no repeatability pass. A lower-count history is not repaid in preparation, later rounds or the final window.

**Static stance, every age.** Retain the actual supported mid-range or higher shallow stance: lead-side hand lightly on the individually fitting stable wall, free hand at hip, whole front foot/rear forefoot grounded. P1 one combined rehearsal at most 3 s per lead, plus 5 s entry, 5 s standing side/hand change, 2 s bilateral transition, 2 s bilateral hold and 5 s exit. S1 one combined set D at most 5 s per lead or L at most 3 s, plus 10 s standing side/hand change and 15 s setup/controlled entry/final exit; at least 60 s recovery, easy 2–3/10 and normal breathing. Preserve each lead’s actual smaller seconds independently; packets 1/2/3/4/5 per lead take the lower of that ceiling and the mode reference. For example recent left 1/right 3 gives S1 1+3+10+15=29 s in D or L, not two full 5 s holds. P1 is 1+3+19=23 s. Quiet P1 uses its 10 s standing packet with zero split entries. Independently suitable first-high S1 counts its entries inside the one combined set; if entry is unsuitable, stop and defer that role. Static holds neither overwrite bilateral squat history nor clear dynamic/unsupported work.

**Hip, every age.** One familiar arms-crossed bodyweight hinge: 3 s hips back/1 s stand, 5 s setup/exit, at least 5 good reps in reserve and 60 s recovery. D ages9–11:3 reps;12–14:4;15–18:4. L:2/3/3 respectively. Familiar two-DB RDL is D only, one set with the same age repetition ceilings, 3 s lowering/1 s stand, 4 s familiar pickup, 4 s set-down and 2 s clearance, at least 5 good reps in reserve and 90 s recovery. One DB in each hand, palms inward, long arms, weights close to thighs, soft knees and actual comfortable range from a fitting elevated parking station. Retain actual kg per DB and total; no forced floor touch or new load. Independently established pickup/top-start/hinge/set-down handling and the most recent compatible loaded record are required. A first OR06 loaded lesson is not familiar handling; later actual bodyweight hip work governs over old DBs. Choose eligible BW before pickup or defer. Complete 1/2/3-rep cap packets preserve actual smaller counts in either booking. Unknown longitudinal BW count may use at most 2 only after independently current familiar control/setup is established; an actual 1-rep record governs. This is not first unfamiliar hinge instruction.

**Push/pull/brace, every age.** Push one familiar incline set D3/4/4 or L2/3/3 (young/reference/older), 2 s lower/1 s press, 5 s setup, at least 5 good reps in reserve, 60 s recovery; retain actual stable support height and foot position. Bench row every age D4 each side or L2 each, 1 s pull/1 s top/2 s lower, 10 s side change plus 10 s handling, 60 s recovery and at least 5 good reps in reserve with the actual familiar DB. Opposite hand AND knee stay on the fitting bench. Independently familiar suspension replaces the whole row set: every age D4 or L3 bilateral reps, 2 s lower/1 s pull, 5 s setup, 60 s recovery, at least 5 good reps in reserve; approximately 70-degree body angle to the floor only where it is the actual retained qualified setup, with verified anchors/grip/body line. No unavailable bench grants suspension handling. Heel taps every age D2 each or L1 each, fixed vertical arms and alternating bent-leg contact/return, 2 s out/2 s back, 10 s setup and 60 s recovery; retain actual target/range and quiet breathing trunk.

Supported breathing replaces the entire brace set: every age/mode at most 4 comfortable cycles, nominal 2 s in/3 s out, 20 s setup/exit, 40 s total plus 15 s quiet recovery. Lower legs rest on a fitting support; both arms assume/reach the comfortable position together, no alternating arm sequence, heel drive, hip lift or breath hold. Exact smaller cycle caps preserve actual recent work. Independent floor transfer, leg support and comfortable bilateral arm action govern first counted instruction. Retained low support packets keep L counts in D (including suspension 3 bilateral), and exact 1/2/3/4 ceilings preserve still smaller work without changing handling/rest. Complete asymmetric row packets select 0–4 actions per side, heel packets 0–2, each capped by the mode reference; total repetitions are left plus right. Keep the original tempo, handling and side-change allowance when any action remains. Both sides zero means no set or handling. No omitted side is repaid on the other side, and independently suitable entry still governs. If dose history is unknown but the role is independently familiar, use at most 2 push/suspension reps, 1 row rep each, 1 heel action each or 1 breathing cycle; this is a named current planning reduction, not a fabricated prior record. Missing one role does not remove the others. Unfamiliar loaded handling is deferred; no extra physical screening set selects a route.

**Known skill with missing dose history.** Independently eligible main movement with unknown longitudinal opportunity count uses one original counted opportunity (or is omitted), keeping its actual approach, direction and selected pause context. Historical count remains null; this is a conservative current planning cap, not proof of a prior one-opportunity dose or of a reduction from known work. There is no added E0 or opposite-side credit. An actual known smaller/zero count or restriction still governs; missing attendance is not an invented completed zero-dose record.

For currently familiar mid/high stance with actually suitable support, depth and controlled entry/exit but unknown historical hold seconds on a lead, both P1 and S1 use at most 1 s on that eligible lead. The other lead follows its own actual smaller ceiling. Keep unknown historical duration null and do not relabel the task first-high. This uses the existing complete one-second lead packets and unchanged handling/rest. A known zero or currently ineligible lead does not permit the positive both-lead stance packet in this lesson; select eligible quiet P1 and defer S1 while preserving other independently useful roles. First-high remains a separately eligible counted instruction path and preserves any applicable actual smaller history.

Direct retained jogging-stop/one-second exit evidence needs the actual controlled corresponding jogging stop, repeatable exact same-context/direction/intent one-second task, comfortable ordinary walking/turning and current suitability. It does not require reconstruction of an older walking-stop or two-second record. This does not waive the actual walking-stop/easy-jog component gate for a first new terminal jogging-stop lesson or permit first jogging stopping and a first exit together.
workload_narrative:
Count the complete resolved base and both targets, including their setup/entry units. P1 actual left/right static holds and bilateral finish remain separate from S1; quiet P1 has zero split entries. P2 is one straight component action, zero assessed exits. E1 opportunity 1 is already inside D3/2 or L2/1 and actual smaller prefixes; context changes never add E0. Record first/retained 1 s, full 2 s, terminal and omitted slots separately by direction. Approach distance, 2 m assessed ordinary exits, outward clearance and outside returns remain different quantities; planning path ceilings are not completed travel. Exact braking/walking contacts, actual kg and athlete outcomes remain null until observed.

When all independently eligible roles are performed, Strength has five sets: static stance as knee/unilateral, hip, push, pull and brace. Side holds/actions belong within their combined set. Counts do not prove recovery; read the Week2 review and actual recent workload, including OR10 knee loading, OR06/09 impact/throw response, sport and separate tumbling. Hand support, DB handling, pressing, pulling and brace share upper-body demand even though their movement histories remain independent. There is no additional squat strength set, physical finisher, hidden load test or fault repayment.
final_tumbling:
Standard75–78 water/readiness;78–84 explain the actual selected pause and direction;84–88 record independent Strength choices and response;88–90 transfer. Compressed55–57 water/readiness;57–60 record/handoff. Every age adds zero physical sets in this final athletic window.

The precise separate 30-minute Body Control/Tumbling session is unresolved. Pass on actual braking/exit attempts by direction and pause, stability/faults, stance seconds/entries, hip handling/load/count, upper-body support/grip and brace response, recent impact and attention. Its coach independently verifies the actual linked skill, landing/support prerequisites, mats, space and staffing. The handoff does not assign zero tumbling workload or clear advanced skills, inversion, rebound or reactive cutting; it is not a completed separate prescription.
coach_record: Record source/date/task/role of actual relevant evidence before selecting demand. Distinguish first 1 s from retained 1 s and full-pause first instruction; record each direction separately without reconstructing unnecessary older history. Log actual P1/P2 completion/omission, every numbered main opportunity including faults/partial work, real pause, approach, direction, ordinary clearance and return issues. Keep exact left/right stance hold seconds and entries, current hip variation/load/handling/repetitions, independent push/row/brace setup and actual smaller counts. Plans and today's first observation never become a historical repeatability record automatically. OR13 and OR20 receive only the precise controlled variant observed; next offering OR12 keeps its separate objective. Record unresolved domains and the suitable next teaching opportunity without making the athlete repeat all completed modules.
review_status: Source and independent written programming reviews PASS. See or_11_review.md, or_11_programming_critique.md and or_11_check_results.json for the daily evidence, numeric status and exact coverage. Written review does not establish actual operating release or the separate tumbling prescription.

P1.variant: Split-Squat Isometric Hold — supported-bodyweight-mid-range plus supported bilateral finish — explicit orientation composite
P1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Each lead holds3s. Use light wall contact with the hand on the front-leg side; free hand at hip. No pushing to an end range.
P1.notes: One composite cycle:5s entry/setup,3s left-lead hold,5s standing side change,3s right-lead hold,2s return to bilateral base,2s supported soft-knee finish,5s exit to the adjacent queue. These25s include both sides and the bilateral finish; do not repeat the cycle for each side. This is one brief P1 rehearsal, so inter-set rest is not applicable; actual P1-to-P2 gap is calculated in the session clock. Later S1 has its separate 60 s recovery rule.

S1.variant: Split-Squat Isometric Hold — supported-bodyweight-mid-range
S1.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2–3/10; one5s hold per lead with normal breathing, well before shaking/strain. Light wall contact, same declared comfortable depth; no external load.
S1.notes: One combined both-side set, not two sets. Two counted holds×5s +10s stand/change lead/support hand +15s total initial setup/controlled entry and final exit = 35s. The hold clock begins only in the assigned position; entry and exit are counted actions, not extra dynamic split-squat repetitions.

age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

records.name: Walking lunge with rotation/reach
records.purpose: Access comfortable split position, front-leg control and coordinated reach.

card_mapping_status.limit: A lunge matrix is related content, not approval for this precise forward-step/reach/return task.

records.setup: Forward step within a 1 m span, then return after each rep. Reach toward the front knee with a small comfortable trunk turn. First visit uses thigh contact and no rotation.
cues: Use a stable split base; lower only as far as controlled.
Turn gently toward the front leg and return tall.
common_errors: Forced depth or twisting over a painful knee.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or instability; use smaller split-stance bend if comfortable, otherwise omit and record.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable split position on both sides with stable foot pressure and smooth return.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral lunge with reach
records.purpose: Access comfortable lateral hip shift and stable foot pressure.

verified_local_names: Lateral Lunge to Rotational Reach Flow
card_mapping_status.limit: The related flow includes rotation; this plain reach requires exact variant review.

records.setup: Step sideways within a 0.75 m span; shift into that hip, reach toward the thigh and return. First visit keeps hands on thigh and a shallow shift.
cues: Sit gently into the stepping hip.
Reach only with controlled trunk position.
common_errors: Chasing depth or lifting support foot unexpectedly.
stop_rules: Stop for unstable foot, discomfort or uncontrolled return.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable lateral shift and return both sides without forced depth.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.

records.name: A-march
records.purpose: Rehearse no-flight reciprocal rhythm and balanced support.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 69 is a review-state candidate with longer travel lanes. Short bay passes need exact profile review. Basic in-place march is a declared regression, not an exact A-March result.

records.setup: Two 1.6 m forward passes inside the bay. Return only after completing a pass. First visit stays in place.
cues: Stand over the support foot; opposite arm and leg.
Place the foot close beneath you.
stop_rules: Stop for balance, comfort or rhythm failure; use basic walking march with same or smaller dose, logged as changed variant.

competency_rule.observe: Controlled actual support/exchange; neither march variant proves sprint competence.

competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

full.variant: Mastered traveling A-March in two short bay passes

execution_segments.name: Four alternating march steps on first pass
Four alternating march steps on second pass

full.tempo: 2 s per march step; 2 s per short ordinary return. One cycle is one left plus one right step.
full.effort: Easy and conversational; no maximal speed, height, stretch or fatigue target.

rest.within_set: Only the pauses, resets and walking returns explicitly included in execution_segments.
rest.after_set: Use the row transition and next demonstration. Waiting waves add no repetitions. Extra required rest uses visible contingency, then an explicit reduction/revision.

full.other_contact_accounting: No intentional flight; ordinary support/steps are not scored plyometric landings.
full.prerequisite: Mastered no-flight support/exchange and reciprocal arms; exact shortened delivery still requires profile review.
full.count_definition: One left or right march step is one primary count. A left-right cycle is two steps and is retained separately as bilateral_march_cycles; walking resets are excluded.

count_reconciliation.calculation: 4 left + 4 right = 8 individual march steps, equivalent to 4 left-right cycles; return steps excluded.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.landing_event_unit: One landing event after flight; bilateral landing is one event involving two feet.
contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.

contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

records.setup: Tiny forward steps within 1 m; walk back after the pass. First visit stays in place with both feet available for balance.
cues: Small comfortable foot action beneath hips.

stop_rules: Stop for foot/ankle discomfort, uncontrolled impact or lost rhythm; use no-flight option only when comfortable.

records.name: Squat-to-stand with overhead reach — concluding check
records.purpose: Observe knee/hip/trunk organization through a comfortable sequence.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. Assigned order is left then right. Current exact dose/profile eligibility remains unverified. The OR thigh-supported partial version remains an explicitly different modification pending variant review.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

competency_rule.observe: Observe actual sequence, foot pressure and control; not a loaded squat or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.change: Easy jog in place and shortened bay-contained travel replace starting-distance layout.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Keep purpose with no crossing or long queue travel.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Exact delivery mapping and measured footprint require review.

reviewable_modifications.change: Stationary bear-position limb unloads replace traveling bear crawl in the familiar composite.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Five sequential slow crawlers per lane cannot be treated as simultaneous overlapping athletes.
reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Purpose-preserving proposal; exact composite and facility delivery remain unapproved.

reviewable_modifications.change: B/C ordered slots perform and record only mastered A-March; compact/OR omit them.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Do not invent an unverified B-march, hip-opening march or C-skip.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: B/C identity/delivery remains unresolved; short A-March profile also needs review.

reviewable_modifications.change: Familiar concluding squat-to-stand now uses four full or two compact complete 8-second LEFT-then-RIGHT reach cycles. Compact hinge remains two reps; OR01 compact remains one observed hinge and one partial squat cycle.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Preserve both source-assigned reaches, safe control and ordered three-wave observation within 720/420 seconds. This explicitly reduces the philosophy full starting dose of five to four; compact squat count changes from three ambiguous cycles to two complete cycles. The philosophy permits scaled repetitions.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Coach-review adaptation of repetition count and delivery, not publication or operational approval. Brief readiness observations do not pass competence; finish required evidence in instructional work.

reviewable_modifications.change: First-visit flow, reach, descent and rhythm use explicitly simpler/no-flight components.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Teach recognizable components honestly instead of pretending reminder demos teach every complex action.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: If actual essential instruction exceeds contingency, mark REVISE and use longer instructional base or another justified booking change.

provenance.source_status: Local authored/research candidates only. No live canonical approval, endorsement or actual athlete result claimed.

validation.arithmetic_status: PASS: 16 ordered records; three explicit age bands; four doses/profile clocks; individual segment sums; group demo/work/wave/transition sums; contiguous 720/420-second bases; concluding hinge/squat order; exactly 180 seconds reserved for two target tasks.
unresolved: Measured floor footprint, body fit, sightlines and separate target corridors
Exact published card/variant/delivery eligibility and live facility approval
Observed timing with 15 actual athletes and unfamiliar transitions
Separate tumbling and whole-day recovery budget
not_inferred: Five-day offering is not five hard attendance days or 20 required on-ramp visits.
Preparation does not automatically grant any main entry route.
validation.count_accounting_status: PASS: all 192 age/profile dose objects have explicit primary count units; included numeric doses reconcile through segment primary-unit contributions; bilateral landings retain event/foot distinction; null unknown contact counts remain null; override routes resolve explicit dose/rest/profile references or explicit zero-dose omission.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.

standard_D.variant: Stop, Pause and Announced Walking Exit — first 1s, walking approach
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight; ordinary deliberate walking, about 2/10. The exit is ordinary walking at about 2/10, with relaxed natural arms; no cutting, sprinting or output contest.
standard_D.notes: One complete numbered opportunity per set; opportunity 1 includes the first selected instruction/current check. Hold 1 s only after a genuine controlled bilateral stop, then the opening step and ordinary 2 m exit, followed by the separate quiet 2 s finish. Both pause contexts retain the 20 s action/clearance and 45 s return envelope. The saved second is clearance slack, never another step quota, faster release or extra effort. If balance needs longer, restore/retain a suitable held task and record the actual pause; do not race the cue.
